name: Topic particle
meaning: Frames the sentence topic or contrasts it with another topic.
shape: Consonant (batchim) ➔ 은 (학생은). Vowel ➔ 는 (학교는).

examples.en: As for the teacher, he or she is at the hospital.
As for the apple, it is delicious.

name: Subject particle
meaning: Highlights or identifies the grammatical subject, often as new information.
shape: Consonant ➔ 이 (학생이). Vowel ➔ 가 (학교가).

examples.en: The friend is at the library.

name: Object particle
meaning: Marks the noun directly affected by an action verb.
shape: Consonant ➔ 을 (책을). Vowel ➔ 를 (커피를).

name: Destination or time
meaning: Marks a destination, a static location, or a specific time. Does not mark the place of an action.
shape: Attaches directly to the noun regardless of batchim (학교에, 병원에).

name: Place of action
meaning: Marks where an action occurs or the place from which movement begins.
shape: Attaches directly to the noun regardless of batchim (학교에서, 병원에서).

examples.en: I eat a meal at a restaurant.
I read a book at the library.

name: To be
meaning: Copular endings attach directly to nouns to equate the subject with a noun.
shape: Consonant ➔ 이에요 (학생이에요). Vowel ➔ 예요 (학교예요). Formal is always 입니다.

name: Existence and possession
meaning: Expresses existence, location, availability, or possession depending on context.
shape: Particles before it follow batchim rules (이 for consonant, 가 for vowel). 있다/없다 themselves don't change based on previous words.

examples.en: There is a cat at home.

name: Short negation
meaning: Neutral short negation. Placed directly before a verb or adjective.
shape: Batchim does not affect this rule. It is simply placed before the word.

examples.en: I do not eat the meal.

name: Inability
meaning: Expresses inability caused by skill, circumstances, or external limits.
shape: Batchim does not affect this rule. It is simply placed before the verb.

name: Present tense
meaning: The standard polite-casual present ending used in everyday conversation.
shape: Depends on the final vowel of the stem, not batchim. ㅏ/ㅗ ➔ 아요, others ➔ 어요, 하 ➔ 해요.

name: Past tense
meaning: Marks a past action, completed event, or past state.
shape: Depends on the final vowel of the stem, not batchim. ㅏ/ㅗ ➔ 았어요, others ➔ 었어요, 하 ➔ 했어요.

name: Future tense
meaning: Expresses a plan, intention, expectation, or prediction.
shape: Consonant ➔ -을 거예요. Vowel ➔ -ㄹ 거예요. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -거예요.

examples.en: I will read a book tomorrow.

name: Polite request
meaning: A polite everyday request or instruction. Can also honor the subject.
shape: Consonant ➔ -으세요. Vowel ➔ -세요. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -세요 (ㄹ drops).

name: Formal command
meaning: A formal directive common in notices, announcements, tests, and official instructions.
shape: Consonant ➔ -으십시오. Vowel ➔ -십시오. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -십시오 (ㄹ drops).

name: Let’s
meaning: A formal or neutral suggestion meaning 'let us'.
shape: Consonant ➔ -읍시다. Vowel ➔ -ㅂ시다. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -ㅂ시다 (ㄹ drops).

name: Shall we?
meaning: Invites the listener’s opinion, proposes a joint action, or offers to do something.
shape: Consonant ➔ -을까요?. Vowel ➔ -ㄹ까요?. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -까요?.

examples.en: Shall we eat a meal together?

name: And / then
meaning: Links equal actions or descriptions without necessarily showing cause.
shape: Attaches directly to the stem regardless of batchim (먹고, 가고, 만들고).

examples.en: I eat a meal and drink coffee.
I meet a friend and go home.

name: Because / then
meaning: Shows a reason or a natural sequence. Cannot be used with commands.
shape: Depends on vowel harmony, not batchim. ㅏ/ㅗ ➔ 아서, others ➔ 어서.

examples.en: I am tired, so I rest.
My stomach hurts, so I go to the hospital.
It rains, so I stay at home.

name: But / although
meaning: Introduces a contrast while acknowledging the first statement.
shape: Attaches directly to the stem regardless of batchim (먹지만, 가지만, 만들지만).

examples.en: It was expensive, but I bought it.
I ate a meal, but I am hungry.

name: If / when
meaning: Expresses a condition or a repeated 'when' relationship.
shape: Consonant ➔ -으면. Vowel ➔ -면. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -면.

examples.en: If it rains, I will not go.
If I have a lot of money, I will buy a house.
If you get time, please contact me.

name: Intention / plan
meaning: Shows an intention, plan, or action that is about to begin.
shape: Consonant ➔ -으려고 하다. Vowel ➔ -려고 하다. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -려고 하다.

examples.en: I plan to read a book.
I intend to meet a friend.
I plan to make a cake.

name: Want to
meaning: Expresses the speaker’s own desire to do an action.
shape: Attaches directly to the stem regardless of batchim (먹고 싶다, 가고 싶다).

examples.en: I want to go to Korea.
I want to watch a movie.

name: Purpose of movement
meaning: States the purpose of movement. Used with movement verbs like 가다/오다.
shape: Consonant ➔ -으러. Vowel ➔ -러. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -러.

examples.en: I go in order to eat lunch.
I go to the park to exercise.
I came to meet a friend.

name: Try / experience
meaning: Means to try an action or to have experienced it.
shape: Depends on vowel harmony, not batchim. ㅏ/ㅗ ➔ 아 보다, others ➔ 어 보다.

examples.en: Please try putting on these clothes.
I have been to Jeju Island.
I have tried eating Korean food.

name: Permission
meaning: Asks for or grants permission; literally means that doing the action is okay.
shape: Depends on vowel harmony, not batchim. ㅏ/ㅗ ➔ 아도 되다, others ➔ 어도 되다.

name: Prohibition
meaning: Expresses prohibition or strong advice not to do something.
shape: Consonant ➔ -으면 안 되다. Vowel ➔ -면 안 되다. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -면 안 되다.

examples.en: You must not take photos here.

name: After
meaning: Indicates that the first action is completed before the second action begins.
shape: Consonant ➔ -은 후에. Vowel ➔ -ㄴ 후에. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -ㄴ 후에 (ㄹ drops).

examples.en: Please take medicine after eating a meal.
I play games after doing homework.
I eat a meal after washing my hands.

name: Before
meaning: The following action happens before the action nominalized with -기.
shape: Attaches directly to the stem regardless of batchim (먹기 전에, 가기 전에).

examples.en: I wash my hands before eating a meal.
I read a book before sleeping.
I studied Korean before coming to Korea.

name: Can / cannot
meaning: Expresses ability or possibility to do an action.
shape: Consonant ➔ -을 수 있다. Vowel ➔ -ㄹ 수 있다. ㄹ-batchim ➔ -수 있다.

examples.ko: 저는 매운 음식을 먹을 수 있어요.

name: Realization / admiration
meaning: A soft spontaneous reaction to newly noticed information.
shape: Attaches directly to the stem. If the stem ends in ㄹ-batchim, the ㄹ drops (만드네요).

name: Surprise / discovery
meaning: Shows discovery. -군요 is explicit, -네요 is softer. Verbs use -는군요.
shape: Verbs take -는군요 (ㄹ-batchim drops). Adjectives take -군요 directly.

examples.en: You eat a lot of food, I see.

name: I think / it seems
meaning: Softens a guess or uncertain opinion rather than stating it as a fact.
shape: Action verbs ➔ -는 것 같다 (ㄹ drops). Adjectives: Consonant ➔ -은 것 같다, Vowel ➔ -ㄴ 것 같다.

examples.en: I think that movie is interesting.

examples.ko: 이 옷이 조금 작은 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think these clothes are a bit small.

name: While / Simultaneous Actions
meaning: Shows that two actions happen at the same time, usually by the same subject.

examples.english: I study while listening to music.
I study while listening to music.
I study while listening to music.

name: Intention / Plan
meaning: Expresses intention, a plan, or something the speaker is about to do.

examples.english: I am planning to study abroad in Korea.
I am planning to study abroad in Korea.
I am planning to study abroad in Korea.

name: After Doing
meaning: Means “after doing” and emphasizes that the first action is completed before the second begins.

examples.english: I drank coffee after eating.
I drank coffee after eating.
I drank coffee after eating.

name: Before Doing
meaning: Means “before doing” and places one action before another.

examples.english: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
I brush my teeth before going to bed.
I brush my teeth before going to bed.

name: Because / Since
meaning: Gives a reason or cause. It is common when the second clause is a command, suggestion, or invitation.

examples.english: Because it is raining, take an umbrella.
Because it is raining, please take an umbrella.
Because it is raining, please take an umbrella.

name: Because / So / And Then
meaning: Shows a reason or a natural sequence.

examples.english: I went to bed early because I was tired.
I went to bed early because I was tired.
I went to bed early because I was tired.

name: Guess / Prediction
meaning: Expresses a guess, impression, or prediction: “it seems,” “I think,” or “probably.”

examples.english: It looks like it will snow tomorrow.
It looks like it will snow tomorrow.
It looks like it will snow tomorrow.

name: If / When
meaning: Expresses a condition. Depending on context, it can mean “if” or “when.”

examples.english: If you have time, let’s go together.
If you have time, let’s go together.
If you have time, let’s go together.

name: Try / Experience
meaning: Means “try doing” or “have tried/experienced doing.”

examples.english: I tried kimchi.
I tried kimchi.
I tried kimchi.

name: Can / Cannot
meaning: Expresses ability, possibility, or impossibility.

examples.english: I can read Korean.
I can read Korean.
I can read Korean.

name: When
meaning: Indicates the time when something happens or happened.

examples.english: I liked soccer when I was young.
I liked soccer when I was young.
I liked soccer when I was young.

name: While Doing / Interruption
meaning: Shows that one action was in progress and then another action occurred.

examples.english: I fell asleep while studying.
I fell asleep while studying.
I fell asleep while studying.

name: Progressive Action
meaning: Shows an action currently in progress: “be doing.”

examples.english: I am reading a book now.
I am reading a book now.
I am reading a book now.

name: Come To / End Up
meaning: Expresses a change of situation, result, or something that came to happen.

examples.english: I came to learn Korean.
I came to learn Korean.
I came to learn Korean.

name: Because / Formal Reason
meaning: Gives a reason in a slightly more formal or written style.

examples.english: I went to bed early because I had an exam.
I went to bed early because I had an exam.
I went to bed early because I had an exam.

name: Have Ever / Past Experience
meaning: Expresses that someone has had an experience before.

examples.english: I have been to Korea.
I have been to Korea.
I have been to Korea.

name: Purpose of Movement
meaning: Expresses going or coming for the purpose of doing an action.

examples.english: I went to meet my friend.
I went to meet my friend.
I went to meet my friend.

name: Realization / Soft Surprise
meaning: Expresses surprise, admiration, or newly realized information.

examples.english: Oh, it is really cold.
Oh, it is really cold.
Oh, it is really cold.

name: Might / May
meaning: Expresses uncertain possibility: “might,” “may,” or “possibly.”

examples.english: I might be late today.
I might be late today.
I might be late today.

name: Seems / I Think
meaning: Expresses an opinion, guess, or impression.

examples.english: He seems to be a student.
He seems to be a student.
He seems to be a student.
